raw.Title: Missal (Use of Beauvais)
raw.Subtitle: Missalis Belvacensis
raw.Reconstruction Summary:
The leaf is from the third volume of a 3-volume Missal given to Beauvais Cathedral by a former canon, Robert de Hangest, shortly before his death on 3 November 1356 so that he would be commemorated every year on the date of his death. The Missal formed part of the Cathedral Library for several centuries until the Napoleonic period when the Missal and other works and relics were removed. While the first and second volumes have yet to surface, the third volume of the Missal (comprising 308 leaves) passed through several hands of ownership. In 1942 it was dismembered with a portion sold to Otto F. Ege. He contributed 42 leaves to specimen sets he compiled and marketed as "Fifty Original Leaves from Medieval Manuscripts". The Missal leaves are listed as no. 15 of the 50 chosen exemplars.
In 1981, this leaf came onto the market, sold by Maggs Bros, London, to the Friends of the Australian National University Library. It is the 111th surviving fragment of the Missal to be identified, the first to be located in Australia.
Contents: Written for use in the liturgy of Beauvais. Text with musical annotation (square musical notation on a 4-line stave) contains the Mass for the fourth Sunday after Easter (including the Credo, Offertory, Secret, Preface, Communion and Postcommunion) and the Introit of the Mass for the fifth Sunday after Easter. 
Decoration: Three 2-line and one 1-line initials ornamented in gold and colours (blue and pink) heightened with white penwork. The large initials have graceful long descenders with interlaced terminals and foliate extensions. Two 2-line initials with geometric penwork in black ink.

reconstruction.title: Graduale Aboense: a documented surviving subset
reconstruction.description: An Åbo-use gradual dated 1397–1406. These are separate source-backed continuity components, not a newly discovered codex or an inferred global page order.
reconstruction.historical_origin: Åbo/Turku liturgical use; production attribution and date derive from the Finnish catalogue and prior scholarship.
reconstruction.dimensions: Surviving Swedish catalogue dimensions around 33 × 23 cm, sometimes trimmed; original untrimmed size is not inferred.
reconstruction.liturgical_function: Gradual: chants for the Mass, including the temporal cycle and saints' feasts.
reconstruction.credits: National Library of Finland; National Archives of Sweden; Toivo Haapanen; Ilkka Taitto's published Graduale Aboense (2002).

config.status: Exploratory pilot, not a preregistered accuracy claim. Version1.1 preserves predictors/weights and adds post-review target controls, duplicate/genre guards and explicit placeholder-content handling.
config.method_selection: On development books, maximize same-genre book-macro MRR; require at least0.02 improvement over metadata on development AND calibration before adopting a more complex method. No test-book tuning.
config.threshold_selection: Maximize F1 on catalogue-label calibration pairs only; ties prefer fewer false positives then higher threshold. Not probability calibration.
config.evaluation: Whole-codex split; leave one physical record out as query; identical within-split galleries; separate same-genre ablation; expected tie-aware metrics; book-macro bootstrap.

limitations: Distinct catalogue codex labels can still contain errors or cross-label identities; these are provisional reference labels, not expert gold.
Only four test book groups are expected; book-bootstrap intervals are descriptive and unstable with few groups.
Physical record separation removes self/capture duplicates, but each source row may contain more than one leaf.
Catalogue attributes may be copied from prior grouping, so metadata can leak identity indirectly despite the feature whitelist.
Generic ImageNet features may learn capture/provider/colour shortcuts; raw/cropped and same-genre ablations do not eliminate all confounding.
Overlap of catalogue content terms is not proof of identical chant text, melody or textual continuity.
No independently adjudicated different-scribe handwriting dataset or reliable probability calibration was secured.
Pretrained data exposure cannot be audited fully. No model was trained or fine-tuned here.
Strong discovery claims are prohibited by these limitations and the unread target-specific later scholarship.

iteration_provenance.changes: Upstream ingestion corrected Beauvais title/placeholder contents and refreshed provenance. story.title: A book becomes a wrapper
story.text: After the Reformation, parchment leaves from medieval books were reused around administrative accounts. Later archival division placed related material in different Nordic collections. Surviving notes tell both medieval and early modern histories.

story.title: A convincing wrong answer
story.text: The first metadata check ranked a published different-book pair uniquely first. Matching script, notation and dimensions were insufficient. That failure became a test case rather than a discovery.

story.title: What the machine can offer
story.text: The pipeline ranks inspectable comparisons using metadata, image layout and a frozen visual encoder. Known associations test retrieval. Uncertain suggestions remain hypotheses requiring textual, codicological and scholarly scrutiny.

story.title: A reconstruction with limits
story.text: The reading sequence shows only catalogue-supported continuities in an already studied gradual. Separate components, unplaced leaves and unknown gaps remain visible. The result demonstrates a method, not the recovery of an unknown complete book.

Two visible antiphon incipits agree with the office sequence in Hallqvist2020 edited C435, printedp6/PDF53. The higher-resolution invitatory comparison now distinguishes edited C435, its apparatus-reported manuscript state and edited C23 (PDF67).

An older Finnish IV157 description already places Swedish account48/ChristiernPhilipssons1610 between Helsinki ff7and8. The pinned CSV uniquely maps that description to Fr10370. This is contextual published evidence, not a new placement or proof for every Codex1505 leaf.

Two actual C23 source pages were acquired from Uppsala Alvin. A declared ten-site comparison retains eight target-evaluable word/structure sites and two unavailable target sites; corrected text, cancelled text and editorial reports remain separate.
Supporting Fr10370 context now has literal verse-prefix/suffix evidence for source-image2→3 order. This improves intrinsic orientation without proving a new relationship involving Fr8994.

The raw MPO note for Fr 8994 describes it as similar to Ant 99 and Helsinki Ant 156/157, cites Taitto 2001, pp. 161–168, and also points to Fr 1385. This is a prior catalogue similarity claim; it does not state that Fr 8994 and Fr 20274 are the same codex.

The updated official F.m.IV.173 record lists Ant 99 as a suggested relationship within a broader stylistic/liturgical group; it does not call Ant 99 a proven same-codex member. This is published prior art for a possible wider production relationship, not direct identity evidence.

The official F.m.IV.157 entry places the St Olaf office at fol. 8 and records opening-signature notation '[k] iiijr - k [v]'; Fr 8994's catalogue foliation is '1r IIII; 1v k'. This is a possible correspondence to test against images, not an established link.

E32 inspected the local first Fr 8994 capture: a source-linked red four-stroke upper-margin mark is consistent with the catalogue's IIII transcription. This checks one visible mark only; side orientation and the paired k are not independently established.
against: Office identity and broad square notation are not unique. No verified physical adjacency or melody/variant alignment found.
The short comparison established no distinctive variant: agreement with a published office sequence is shared liturgical evidence, not independent evidence for the proposed physical association.

The apparent absence of separate pium and Matri…condolentes before procida… agree with the standard edited wording, not a unique book fingerprint. The edition reports different states for C435. No direct inspection of C435 manuscript images is claimed.

No hymn entry is visible between Venite and Immolandus in the inspected continuous target region. This is a written-layout observation; abbreviated practice, different book function or a hymn elsewhere remain alternatives.

No distinctive shared uncorrected C23 reading is established. Seven selected sites give current/standard word or cue agreements; the eighth has a visible C23 hymn entry where the target continuous region has none. These are not eight independent identity features or a transmission tree.

The predeclared Fr10370 boundary ROIs did not pass translation or SIFT/RANSAC registration; the same feature screen also produces small low-inlier fits for the deliberately different 2/3 control. These non-results do not prove different faces but remove no physical ambiguity.

E26's checksum-verified BOMPAC workbook assigns Fr 20274/Ant 99/IV.157 to BOMPAC-912 and Fr 8994/Codex 1505/IV.156 to BOMPAC-5324. This is a published separate reconstruction, but it is research metadata rather than a fresh direct image examination; it does not by itself rule out a more complex relationship.

E27's checksum-verified BOMPAC query puts F.m.IV.173, Ant 242/Fr 29666 and Hy 49/Fr 25592 in BOMPAC-9531, while Ant 99/IV.157 remain in BOMPAC-912. The different reconstruction units clarify the published disagreement but are not fresh image proof.

Walta 2013's indexed excerpt places IV.156, IV.157 and IV.173 in a larger stylistic/production group, but does not say these are one codex. Its categories therefore cannot be treated as a direct contradiction of the narrower BOMPAC reconstruction units.

The official Fragmenta catalogue describes IV.156 and IV.157 as stylistically similar but does not say they are the same codex; Codex 1505 is listed as a suggestion, while other links receive explicit same-codex labels.

The official Fragmenta entry calls Codex 1505 a suggested relation to IV.157, not a demonstrated same-codex member; the possible k/IV signature alignment has not been checked against F.m.IV.157 and Fr 20278 images.

The official F.m.IV.156 catalogue says the opening-signature convention was not infrequent in late-medieval codices and early printed books. The format alone therefore has limited specificity and is not a unique Codex 1505 fingerprint.
reviews.outcome: Still C / unresolved. One local Fr 8994 capture shows a four-stroke red mark consistent with IIII, but the image does not independently establish side mapping, the paired k, or a match with IV.157. The signature format is described as not uncommon; only paired textual and sequence evidence could make this a specific attribution test. No new attribution is established.

supporting: Fr8311 incipit and verse provisionally identify Cantus006537/006537a, agreeing with Septuagesima catalogue contents. Other books in the chant databases have the same chant.
against: A geographically widespread chant does not connect this fragment to Fr1385. This suggestion belongs to the same Ant39 cluster as H08/H10.
Selected decorated initials provide a control for shared ornamental vocabulary; resemblance in these traits is not unique to H02 and cannot identify a book or scribe.

Letter-controlled examples are now retained separately: selected Ant39 A samples differ from the H02 A samples, while the R comparison is incomplete for red fill/lozenges. This local contrast establishes no rarity, common hand or physical exclusion.

The BOMPAC combined reconstruction workbook assigns Fr 8311 to BOMPAC-258 (Ant-39/Codex-1200/FM.IV.159) and Fr 1385 to BOMPAC-912 (Ant-99/FM.IV.157); its raw MPO workbook similarly places the candidate in C-17 and Fr 1385 in singleton F-1385. These are published reconstruction assignments, not fresh image proof or independent adjudication. They weigh against treating the model suggestion as a new same-codex match but do not by themselves disprove physical connection, a shared hand, or broader production context.
reviews.outcome: The checksum-verified BOMPAC datasets place the suggested pair in different reconstruction units and group all three suggestions with Ant 39/Codex 1200. The high model compatibility is therefore not new same-book evidence. Because workbook labels are not a fresh physical examination, retain category C rather than claim rejection.
reviews.next_evidence_needed: Only reopen the same-codex proposal if source-level text, foliation/quire evidence, or diagnostic hand/notation features can test the BOMPAC separation; otherwise treat this as an unresolved model lookalike, not a new discovery.

Its raw MPO workbook groups the five Codex 1505 fragments as M-1217, Fr 20274–20278 as C-35/Ant-99, and Fr 1385 as singleton F-1385. The raw Fr 8994 note calls it very similar to Ant 99 and the Helsinki Ant 156/157, citing Taitto 2001, pp. 161–168; the Fr 1385 note calls it the same manuscript as Ant 157.
